input.add_to_description: Day 21 ~3 AM: hauled Korvash back to the ledger-house, showed him Tessa (alive, stitching his side) and gave an ultimatum: swear by the dawn bell or Dreg and Gorrak's twenty Tallies are hanged in the yard, Gorrak with them, and Tessa stays regardless. The scorched ledger sits in a new iron chest in the inner room under two grey-cloaks. Ledger-house layout learned by Korvash: east shuttered windows toward the drain-stair, wash-house door on the roof at the north end, bar on the inside of the main door.

entries.text:
They walk you up, and you let your feet drag and your head hang, and you read everything.

Six grey cloaks, one on each side and four behind, spears and short swords, no crossbows. The gate-top walk is wide enough for three abreast, with a low parapet to the right and a sheer drop beyond it. The ledger-house sits at the end like a squat stone chapel. Its east wall has two shuttered windows, both facing the drain-stair side. The wash-house roof door stands at the north end, shut, with a grey cloak on it who stamps his feet against the cold. The main door is oak, banded, and it has a heavy bar on the inside. You hear it lifted as they bring you up.

At the threshold you plant your heels and say it flat and loud, so it carries through the wood. You'll hear his terms, but not before you've seen Tessa alive and whole with your own eyes.

The sergeant drags you in by the elbow, but not roughly. The inner room is warmer than you remember. The stove is lit again, and the lamp burns on the desk, a new one with a brass shade. Tessa sits on a stool by the stove with a bowl of water and a needle, bent over the Foreman's side, stitching. She looks up. Her face is grey and the knot on her skull has turned the colour of a plum, but her hands are steady and her eyes are clear. She sees you, and her mouth moves once, wordless: *Kor.* A guard behind her shifts his spear and she bends back to her work.

The Foreman sits behind the desk in a clean apron with a blanket over his knees. Beside him stands a new iron-bound chest, black with soot at the corners, and on the chest lies the ledger, its edge singed brown and curled. Two grey cloaks flank it. He has the beads in his hand again, but they are not moving.

You start your questions, and he lets you ask the first two. What of the safe-conduct, and how will he honour a term the Tallies have already sworn to? Then he lifts one finger.

"I'm weary, Emberhide," he says mildly. "You are a talker, and tonight talk costs me twenty good soldiers' goodwill. I will not spend another hour on it." He folds his hands. "At the dawn bell, Sergeant Dreg and the twenty spears in my barracks yard will be hanged from the third-gate wall, in view of the mountain, for the conspiracy of listening to a prisoner. Captain Vael will hang beside them. The mender stays regardless. I will keep her until she stops being useful, and you cannot see how long that is." His small gentle voice does not change. "Or you swear, now, and the rope is not used, and I forget a great many things. The term is as I read it. The safe-conduct is withdrawn. That is my last offer."

The bell will ring at about half past six. It is a little after three. You have three hours and a bit, 1 hit point, and your wrists in iron. Tessa's stitching hand has not stopped moving. The ledger lies a long stride from the chest, under the eyes of two grey cloaks. Behind you, the door is barred again.

His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. input.add_to_description: Day 21 ~3:00 AM: Korvash (nat 20 Perception) saw on the way up: Dargan's greataxe with the ember-red sash racked in the ledger-house guard-room by the outer door; Tessa's wash-house door on the gate-top roof still ajar with a thread of lamplight; the new stair shift is six grey-cloaks, not Tally-sworn. ~3:30 AM: the Foreman, bandaged and tired, set a deadline: Gorrak Vael hangs at the dawn bell unless Korvash swears the oath. Tessa is sewing his wounds, her wrists bound in front.

entries.text:
You let them walk you, dragging your feet like a beaten man, and your eyes do the work your hands can't. You count six grey cloaks, not Tally-sworn, none of them men you've seen before. Two carry crossbows and four carry spears. There are three windows on the gate-top walk, all shuttered but one. The bar of the ledger-house door sits on the outside, a heavy beam, with a second smaller bar on the inner side. You have rarely seen a place so ready to keep a thing in.

Then you see two things you did not expect. Through the half-open outer door of the guardroom, racked between two spears against the wall, stands your father's greataxe, with Dargan's ember-red sash still knotted to the haft. And at the far corner of the roof, beyond the wash-line where the red cloth hung, a small door stands ajar with a thread of lamplight under it. Tessa's wash-house door. The grey cloaks have not noticed it, or have not thought it worth a bar.

At the ledger-house door you plant your heels and say it flat, loud enough to carry through the wood. You will hear his terms, and you will see your sister alive and whole with your own eyes before you say one word.

There is a pause. Then the Foreman's small voice, from inside. "Bring him."

Inside, the room is warmer than before. The stove has been fed, and the beams show black where the lamp-fire licked them. The Foreman sits behind the righted desk with his side bound tight and his face grey with fatigue. Tessa sits on a stool at his elbow with her wrists tied in front of her and a needle in her bound hands, stitching the long cut in his sleeve. She looks up when you come in. She has a bruise like a thumbprint on her temple, and her eyes are clear. She nods once. The ledger lies at the Foreman's elbow in a new chest, its scorched corner tucked under a sheet of clean paper.

"Alive, whole, and sewing," says the Foreman. "As you asked." He folds his hands on the beads. "I am a patient man, Emberhide, and I have all night. Ask your questions."

You ask. It is not hard to make him talk, because he likes to be understood. He tells you that the mountain's silver-tin runs thin in the lower shafts, that the Tallies are the only hands he can buy at a price, that he took Gorrak's debt because the man was useful and frightened. He admits nothing about the figure on the page. When you press, he says only that a ledger is a tool, and tools are mended. The minutes slide past. The stove ticks. Tessa's needle clicks. Once, when the Foreman is looking at you, her eyes meet yours and flick toward the shuttered window, then back to her work.

At last he sets down his pen. "Dawn is three hours off, and it is a poor use of a night," he says gently. "Here is my last offer, because I would sooner end this than keep a man hungry. You swear as written. Your sister goes down the road at first light with her mule. If you will not, Captain Vael hangs from the gate-beam at the dawn bell, in front of his own twenty spears, and the little one with the split head beside him." He lifts the pen. "I would rather not. It would be untidy."

It is half past three in the morning. You have 1 hit point, a roomful of grey cloaks, your father's axe racked thirty feet away, and a wash-house door left ajar for you. The Foreman is waiting.

You drag your feet and use the time. There are six grey cloaks around you. Two carry crossbows, and the rest have swords and short spears. Wind comes off the black rock in gusts, and the torches gutter. The ledger-house door is oak, banded in iron, with a heavy bar standing on the inside. You mark all that. Whatever else the walk has to tell you, in the dark and with your head ringing, you miss.

At the door you plant your heels and say it flat and loud, the way you'd tell a wolf where the line is: you'll hear his terms, but you see Tessa alive and whole before you say a word.

The sergeant looks at you with something close to contempt. Then the door opens from inside.

The room is as you left it, the table righted and the stove ticking, with the scorch across the floor. The six spears have gone from the walls and four grey cloaks stand in their place. The Foreman sits behind his desk, his side freshly bound, his eyes red-rimmed and his face carefully serene. At his elbow stands an iron-bound chest with its lid open, and in it, black along the edges, the ledger. Tessa sits on a stool by the stove. A dark bruise runs up her temple. Her hands are bound in her lap, and a needle and a bowl of bloody water stand on the floor by her feet. She looks at you, and her thumb presses once against the stool, twice. The clan's sign: *wait.*

"There," says the Foreman. "Alive and whole, as you asked. I keep my courtesies." He doesn't rise. "You have your answer. Now no more questions, Emberhide. I have had my fill of them tonight, and so have my men. You have also cost me a good guard and half a night's sleep, and you have taught my people to count."

You try to fill the quiet. You ask about the term, about the surety, about the word on the contract. He answers each in a few clipped sentences and no more, and he doesn't take the bait to stretch. He is tired and afraid, and fear has made him tidy. He lays the pen across the page. "The oath, as first written. The year and a day, the surety, the safe-conduct. Tessa leaves at first light. The captain is mine. Swear it now, or I send the mender back to the shaft with the captain and the cripple, and you can swear to the dark."

The four cloaks along the wall have not moved. It is a little after three in the morning, with the dawn bell still three hours off, and he has not given you the time you wanted. You are at 1 hit point and in irons. The Foreman waits, pen above the contract.

input.add_to_description: Day 21 ~3:05 AM: summoned Korvash alone to the ledger-house; refuses further bargaining or reading of terms, holds Tessa at knifepoint by a grey-cloak, gives Korvash until the dawn bell to swear. Six grey-cloaks escort; the scorched ledger sits in a new iron-bound chest beside his desk. Korvash noticed the gate-top layout: shuttered windows, a single barred stair door, and an unwatched wash-house door at the right (east) corner of the roof with the old drain-stair below it.

entries.text:
You drag your feet on the stair and keep your eyes working. It is the herder's habit of counting a pass before you walk it.

Six grey cloaks, two ahead of you, two behind and two at your elbows. Every window on the gate-top walk is shuttered, and a plank bar rides across the stair door at your back. The ledger-house door ahead has a lamp-lit slit under it and one guard on either side. And at the right-hand corner of the roof, beyond the torch-light, the wash-house stands low and dark with its door shut and no one watching it. Below it you can just see the black lip of the drain-stair going down the wall, the old way Tessa meant for you on the night this began.

At the door you plant your heels and say it loud and flat, so it carries through the planks. Tell your Foreman you'll hear his terms, but you'll see Tessa alive and whole before you say a word.

It earns you nothing. The sergeant's face doesn't change. He shoves the door open with his spear butt and pushes you in.

The room is hotter than before. The stove is lit, and the lamp is back on the desk with the Foreman behind it, pale and bandaged under the apron, his fingers moving over the brass beads. Beside his chair stands a new iron-bound chest, still bright where the old one had burned. The scorched ledger sits on top of it, a black-edged corner showing.

Tessa is on the floor at his feet with her hands tied before her and a blade at her throat. A grey cloak holds it there with one hand twisted in her collar. Her eyes are open and clear, and a bruise has bloomed along her jaw. She sees you and she does not speak.

"You asked to see her," the Foreman says, mildly. "There. Whole, and quite able to thread a needle, which is why she lives." He does not smile. "I have stopped reading you my terms, Emberhide. You are a clever man with a clause, and I have learned what it costs me. The terms are as I spoke them, less the mule and the safe-conduct. The oath is sworn tonight, before the dawn bell, or I send the rider to the Stones and I do the other thing to your sister." The beads click once. "I do not hurry. But I do not wait for you either."

Six cloaks are at your back, the stove ticks, and the clouds outside the shutters have begun to grey. The dawn bell is a little over two hours away. You are at 1 hit point, with your wrists in iron and a blade at your sister's throat. What does Korvash do?

input.add_to_description: Day 23 ~3 PM: the freed column from Greyshaft arrives; a crowd of Harrowmere folk, including Aunt Veshra and the drover Hale Orrin, waits there, warned by Ushk's earlier return with the children.

entries.text:
Gorrak gives a short nod. You say you'll bring him to Hale Orrin and Veshra at the Stones, so he can ask for honest pay in his own voice. "We will see whether the drover has ears," he says, and no more. You stretch the stiffness from your shoulders and tell Tessa to budge up. She does, without opening her eyes, and says, "You snore like a landslide." Pip is already asleep against her other side. You sleep with the fire at your feet and the sentries on the rim, and nothing wakes you.

The morning is grey and cold. The column rises, eats what is left of the bread, and goes on down the ore road. The scree gives way to scrub, then to pasture still white at the edges. The children begin to name the hills. By midday someone sees a thread of chimney smoke, and a sound goes through the column that isn't quite a cheer. Ninna's friends, who have been counting heads all morning, start counting the number of days instead.

It's near three in the afternoon when the Border Stones come up out of the haze: three weathered pillars on the high road, where you swore your first oath. Today they are not alone. Half of Harrowmere seems to be there. Drovers, wives, herder families in their good wool, and a handful of the town watch stand in a loose, silent ring on the frozen grass. Ushk's ten spears stand among them, helms off. He must have kept faith: no grey cloak and no hobgoblin has been harmed. Kneeling by the nearest stone is a small, upright old woman in a faded blue shawl with a basket at her knee. She doesn't call out. She just stands up.

Beside her is a broad-shouldered man with a drover's crook, who must be Hale Orrin. Behind them a boy of about twelve, Pell, is holding a small girl's hand. The girl is staring straight at you. It is Wren.

Behind you the column has stopped. The Tally-sworn have taken their helms off, as you told them. Gorrak is at your left, bareheaded and bare-faced, and Dreg and Brun are a step behind him. Tessa's hand has found your sleeve.

Aunt Veshra takes one step forward. The whole crowd is waiting to see what you do.

Korvash plans to introduce Gorrak to him on Day 23 at the Border Stones to ask about honest pay as drover-road escorts. Waits with Veshra and townsfolk at the Stones when the column arrives.
relationships: knows the high road and drovers' needs; friend of [[Aunt Veshra]]
Korvash wants [[Gorrak Vael]] to ask him for honest escort work

entries.text: notebook: created an entry for Hale Orrin; added 2 relationships to Hale Orrin

You tell Gorrak that's what to put to Harrowmere. Hale Orrin knows the high road better than any man living, and you'll bring the captain to him and Veshra at the Stones so he can ask for honest pay in his own voice. Gorrak says nothing, but he doesn't say no.

Then you stand, stretch your shoulders, and tell Tessa to budge up. She does, with a snort that is almost a laugh. For the first time in more years than you care to count, you sleep with your sister's breathing beside you.

The next day is the lowland road: frost on the ruts, then mud, then a thin warm sun. The mountains fall behind you. Around noon the children begin to recognize hills. One girl stops and points, and a boy cries out. By mid-afternoon a few have started to run, and nobody tries to stop them.

Just before five you come over the last rise, and there are the Border Stones, three grey stones against a sky going gold. A crowd is waiting at them. Aunt Veshra stands in front with her shawl pulled tight, small and straight and fierce. Beside her is a weathered man in a drover's coat, who must be Hale Orrin. Behind them are fifty or sixty townsfolk, herders, and parents who have waited here since Ushk brought the first children home. Pell is among them, with Wren on his hip.

The children break from the column like water from a dam. Names are shouted, and the sound goes up into the evening and doesn't stop. Pip stops dead beside you, gripping the hem of your coat. Tessa has gone absolutely still, with one hand over her mouth, looking at Veshra. Veshra is looking at her.

Behind you the Tally spears have halted at your word, helms off, and the townsfolk are looking at them. Gorrak stands beside Dreg, bareheaded, with his burned face to the crowd. Nobody in the crowd moves toward him. Someone near the back spits.

It's a little before five on Day 23. What does Korvash do?

input.add_to_description: Day 23 ~4:48 PM: the freed column from Greyshaft (about 90 hands plus Dreg's 40 Tally spears, Gorrak Vael, Korvash and Tessa) reached the Stones. Ushk and Aunt Veshra, with Hale Orrin and townsfolk, were waiting, word having come ahead of them.

entries.text:
"Then that's what we put to Harrowmere, Captain," you say. Hale Orrin is a drover and knows what the high road needs better than any soldier. You'll bring Gorrak to him and Aunt Veshra at the Stones, and he can ask for honest pay in his own voice.

Gorrak says nothing, but he doesn't say no. You stand, stretch your sore shoulders, and tell Tessa to budge up and make room for a big brother. She does it with a snort. Pip is already asleep between you. You sleep sound, and nobody wakes you with a boot.

The next day is a long walk. The ore road flattens, the snow thins to frost, and the lowlands open below you, grey fields, pale smoke, and a winding river. The children go quiet when they see the first walled steading. Some of them start to run, and the Tallies let them.

You reach the Border Stones at a little before five in the evening. The three weathered pillars stand black against a low gold sky, and a crowd is waiting on the road beyond them. Ushk stands at the front with his helm under his arm and a few of his ten spears at his back. Beside him, small and upright with her shawl pulled tight, is Aunt Veshra. A lean, grizzled drover with a crook in his hand stands at her shoulder. That must be Hale Orrin. Behind them stand half the town, herders and carters and shopkeepers, all silent. Pell is there, and a small girl in a hobgoblin's blanket clings to his hand. Wren.

The freed children see their own people. For a breath nothing moves. Then the whole column breaks, and the road fills with running and crying, names shouted, and mothers on their knees in the frost.

Veshra doesn't run. She looks along the road until she finds you and Tessa side by side, and her hand goes to her mouth. Dreg, behind you, has halted forty spears at the first stone and ordered the helms off, as promised. Gorrak stands at the head of them with his burned face bare. The crowd has seen him, and the silence in it has changed.

What does Korvash do?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).

features: Draconic Ancestry: You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

Breath Weapon: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation. When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
Damage Resistance: You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.
Draconic Ancestry (Red): breath weapon 15 ft cone, DEX save DC 12, 2d6 Fire damage (half on a success); resistance to that damage type

Rage: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor: - You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. - When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table. - You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging. Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again. At level 2: rage damage bonus +2; 2 rages before a long rest.
Unarmored Defense: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

Reckless Attack: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Danger Sense: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

input.add_to_description: Day 23 ~3 PM: the freed column reached the Stones. Korvash plans to leave the Tally-sworn here under his eye while he brings Gorrak to speak to Aunt Veshra and Hale Orrin about honest pay as ore-road and drover guards.

entries.text:
You tell Gorrak the thing to put to Harrowmere is exactly that. Hale Orrin is a drover and knows what the high road needs better than any man, and you'll bring him and Aunt Veshra to the Stones to hear it in Gorrak's own voice. Gorrak says nothing, but he doesn't say no. Then you stand, stretch your shoulders, and go to make room by the fire. "Budge up, Tess," you say, "and make room for a big brother." She does, without opening her eyes, and shoves her cold feet against your leg.

The night passes without a boot at your ribs. The sentries change. Once you wake to the sound of Pip talking in his sleep, reciting sums in Goblin, and Tessa's hand patting his back without waking. In the grey before dawn, the column wakes and moves. Another long day of road, the lowlands opening beneath you in a quilt of frosted fields and chimney smoke.

It's a quarter to three in the afternoon when you see the Border Stones: three weathered standing stones on the high road. You've seen them before with Wren's hand in a stranger's, and your axe at your back.

The road in front of the Stones is not empty. A crowd stands there. Drovers, herd-wives, townsfolk with their cloaks pulled tight, somebody's dog. Word has run ahead of the column, as it always does. At the front, small and straight in her grey shawl, stands Aunt Veshra. Beside her is a lean, weathered man with a drover's crook, who must be Hale Orrin. Pell stands close at her elbow, and beside him a small girl holds his hand and stares up the road with her mouth open. Ninna is there too, with Ushk close behind her, out of his armour, looking uncomfortable.

When they see the column, the crowd goes quiet. Behind you the Tallies have stopped dead, helms in their hands, spears furled. Dreg's jaw is tight. Brun is white. Gorrak has halted a pace behind your shoulder, burned face bare to the afternoon light.

Veshra's eyes are on Tessa. She hasn't yet moved, and her hand has gone to her mouth.

What does Korvash do?
